seed.title: The Royal Scepter & Seed of the Woman
seed.subtitle: From Genesis 3:15 to Revelation 12: The Promised Deliverer's Lineage
seed.description: Trace how the 'Seed of the Woman' announced in Eden narrows through Abraham, the Tribe of Judah, and the house of King David, culminating in the Virgin Birth and eternal reign of Jesus Christ.

steps.stage: 1. The Edenic Promise (c. 1400 BC)
steps.note: The Seed of the woman is promised to crush the serpent's head while having His heel struck.
steps.highlight: Universal hope for fallen humanity.

steps.stage: 2. The Abrahamic Covenant (c. 2000 BC)
steps.note: God promises that all nations of the earth will be blessed through Abraham's offspring; Paul reads that offspring as one Seed, Christ (Galatians 3:16).
steps.highlight: Narrows from humanity to one chosen family.

steps.stage: 3. The Tribal Scepter of Judah (c. 1850 BC)
steps.note: Jacob prophesies that the royal scepter will not depart from Judah until Shiloh comes.
steps.highlight: Narrows from twelve tribes to the royal tribe of Judah.

steps.stage: 4. The Eternal Throne of David (c. 1000 BC)
steps.note: God swears to King David that his descendant will sit upon an everlasting throne as God's Son.
steps.highlight: Narrows from Judah to David's royal house.

steps.stage: 5. The Virgin Birth in Bethlehem (c. 734-700 BC)
steps.note: Matthew reads Isaiah's sign of Immanuel as the virgin birth of Jesus (Matthew 1:22-23) and Micah's ruler from Bethlehem Ephrathah as pointing to His birthplace (Matthew 2:5-6).
steps.highlight: Matthew finds both the how and the where in the prophets.

steps.stage: 6. The Lion of Judah & Reigning Son of Man (AD 30-95)
steps.note: Christ triumphs as the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Revelation 5:5) and at His trial applies Daniel's Son of Man to Himself (Matthew 26:64).
steps.highlight: Christians read the royal promises, from Eden on, as reaching their goal in Christ.

lamb.title: The Passover Lamb & Suffering Servant
lamb.subtitle: From Exodus 12 to Calvary: The Substitutionary Sacrifice
lamb.description: Follow the sacrificial scarlet thread from the Passover blood on Egypt's doorposts, through David's Psalm 22 and Isaiah's Suffering Servant, to Calvary and the throne of the Lamb.

steps.stage: 1. The Bronze Serpent & Passover Lamb (c. 1440 BC)
steps.note: An unblemished lamb with no bones broken shelters Israel by its blood; the lifted bronze serpent heals the dying.
steps.highlight: Salvation through a lifted, unblemished substitute.

steps.stage: 2. Pierced Hands & Divided Garments (c. 1000 BC)
steps.note: David's lament opens with 'My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?' and describes enemies who 'have pierced my hands and feet' and 'cast lots for my clothing'.
steps.highlight: The Gospels quote this psalm at the cross (Matthew 27:46; John 19:24).

steps.stage: 3. Pierced for Our Transgressions (c. 700 BC)
steps.note: The silent Lamb bears the iniquity of us all, is numbered with the transgressors, and is assigned a grave 'with a rich man in His death'.
steps.highlight: The Servant suffers in the place of others.

steps.stage: 4. Thirty Pieces of Silver & The Stricken Shepherd (c. 520 BC)
steps.note: The Shepherd is priced at 30 silver pieces thrown to the potter, and Yahweh says 'they will look on Me, the One they have pierced.'
steps.highlight: Remarkable convergence of passion details.

steps.stage: 5. Accomplished on the Cross (AD 33)
steps.note: Crucified at Passover time, Jesus says, 'It is finished.' Afterwards His legs are not broken and His side is pierced.
steps.highlight: John notes four Scriptures fulfilled in a single afternoon.

priest.title: The Eternal Melchizedek Priest-King
priest.subtitle: From Genesis 14 & Psalm 110 to Hebrews: Uniting Crown and Altar
priest.description: Under the Law of Moses, kings came from Judah and priests came strictly from Levi. Discover how Scripture resolves this tension through the order of Melchizedek and the Resurrection.

steps.stage: 1. Melchizedek Blesses Abraham (c. 2000 BC)
steps.note: Melchizedek, both King of Salem and Priest of God Most High, brings bread and wine and receives tithes from Abraham.
steps.highlight: Establishes a priesthood older and higher than Levi.

steps.stage: 2. The Holy One Will Not See Decay (c. 1000 BC)
steps.note: David trusts that God will not abandon him to Sheol or let His Holy One see decay; Peter says David spoke here as a prophet about the resurrection (Acts 2:30-31).
steps.highlight: Hebrews 7:16 calls Christ a priest 'by the power of an indestructible life'.

steps.stage: 3. The Third-Day Sign of Jonah (c. 760 BC)
steps.note: Three days in the depths followed by third-day deliverance becomes Jesus' signature sign.
steps.highlight: Death conquered on the third day.

steps.stage: 4. Ascended on High at the Father's Right Hand (AD 33-65)
steps.note: Having offered one sacrifice forever, Christ sits down at God's right hand, ever living to intercede for us.
steps.highlight: Crown and priesthood united forever.

temple.title: The Temple, The Cornerstone & Dwelling Presence of God
temple.subtitle: From the Tabernacle & Yom Kippur to the Living Stones
temple.description: Trace how the physical sanctuary in Jerusalem points to Christ as the true Temple, the rejected Cornerstone, and the Mercy Seat where heaven and earth meet.

steps.stage: 1. The Day of Atonement Behind the Veil (c. 1440 BC)
steps.note: Blood brought inside the Holy of Holies and sins confessed over the scapegoat.
steps.highlight: Foreshadows Christ entering heaven once for all.

steps.stage: 2. A House of Prayer for All Nations (c. 960 BC)
steps.note: Solomon prays at the Temple dedication that foreigners from far countries will know God's name.
steps.highlight: The Temple was always meant to draw the nations.

steps.stage: 3. The Rejected Stone Becomes the Cornerstone (c. 950 BC)
steps.note: The stone cast aside by the builders is chosen by God as the chief cornerstone.
steps.highlight: Explains the rejection and vindication of Messiah.

steps.stage: 4. Greater Glory of the Second Temple (c. 520 BC)
steps.note: Haggai promises that God will fill the modest Second Temple with glory: 'The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former.'
steps.highlight: Christians traditionally see this fulfilled when Jesus came to the temple.

covenant.title: The New Covenant & Justification by Faith
covenant.subtitle: From Sinai's Stone Tablets to the Law Written on the Heart
covenant.description: Explore how the Prophets anticipated a new covenant that would not merely command righteousness from the outside, but forgive sin completely and transform the heart from within.

steps.stage: 1. The Prophet Like Moses (c. 1400 BC)
steps.note: Moses promises a future Prophet from among his brethren into whose mouth God will put His words.
steps.highlight: Anticipates the Mediator of a better covenant.

steps.stage: 2. The Just Shall Live by Faith (c. 605 BC)
steps.note: God tells Habakkuk that, unlike the proud, the righteous will live by faith, trusting Him through the coming judgment.
steps.highlight: Quoted in Romans, Galatians, and Hebrews.

steps.stage: 3. The New Covenant Promised (c. 600 BC)
steps.note: God promises to write His law on human hearts and remember their sins no more.
steps.highlight: Enacted by Jesus with the cup at the Last Supper.

steps.stage: 4. Rebuilding David's Tent for the Gentiles (c. 760 BC → AD 49)
steps.note: At the Jerusalem Council, James cites Amos 9 to show that Gentiles are welcomed by grace through faith.
steps.highlight: One covenant family across all nations.

spirit.title: The Outpoured Spirit & New Creation
spirit.subtitle: From Genesis 1 & Ezekiel 36 to Pentecost & Revelation 22
spirit.description: Follow the promise of living water, the indwelling Holy Spirit, and the renewal of all creation from Eden lost to Eden restored.

steps.stage: 1. Water from the Struck Rock (c. 1440 BC)
steps.note: Moses strikes the rock at Horeb and water gushes out for the thirsty camp.
steps.highlight: Paul: 'that rock was Christ'; John links living water with the Spirit (John 7:38-39).

steps.stage: 2. The Spirit Poured Out on All Flesh (c. 800 BC)
steps.note: Joel prophesies the outpouring of the Spirit on sons and daughters—fulfilled on the Day of Pentecost.
steps.highlight: Every believer becomes a temple of the Spirit.

steps.stage: 3. A New Heart & Clean Water (c. 585 BC)
steps.note: God promises to replace His people's heart of stone with a heart of flesh and to put His Spirit within them.
steps.highlight: Widely read as the background to being 'born of water and the Spirit' (John 3:5).

steps.stage: 4. New Heavens, New Earth & Tree of Life (c. 700 BC → AD 95)
steps.note: The curse is abolished, death is swallowed up (Isa 25:8), and the leaves of the Tree of Life heal the nations.
steps.highlight: The grand canonical circle completes.
